material_events.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Part I Item 2 (P5).
material_events.claim: War broke out in the Middle East between Iran and the U.S. and Israel alongside vessel seizures and attacks in regional waterways, causing oil supply disruptions and spot charter rate volatility without a material adverse effect on INSW to date.
quotes: The outbreak of war in the Middle East between Iran and the U.S. and Israel in late February 2026, and the seizures and attacks on vessels travelling through the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden, the Arabian Gulf, and the Strait of Hormuz, have caused supply disruptions and changes in trading patterns in the oil and gas markets and significant volatility in energy prices and spot charter hire rates.
To date, these geopolitical developments have not had a material adverse effect on INSW’s operations, financial condition, results of operations or cash flow.

risks.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Risk Factors, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A, and Q3 2026 earnings release.
risks.claim: INSW derived approximately 82%, 86% and 91% of its TCE revenues in the spot market in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, leaving earnings exposed if historically high charter rates decline.
quotes: In the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, INSW derived approximately 82%, 86% and 91%, respectively, of its TCE revenues in the spot market.

Also, while charter rates for crude tankers and product carriers have increased significantly and remain historically high following the extended disruption to shipping in the Middle East areas noted above, it is unlikely that the charter rates will remain at these historically high levels.

As of October 1, 2026, the Company has 11 vessels on time charter agreements with an average duration of 2.0 years and total future contracted revenues through expiry of approximately $305 million, excluding any applicable profit share.

risks.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A and 2025 Form 10-K Risk Factors.
risks.claim: War in the Middle East and vessel attacks since February 2026 threaten fleet safety, elevate near-term pool voyage expenses via bunker and war-risk premiums, and expose INSW to maritime losses beyond its $1.0 billion per-vessel insurance coverage.
quotes: The outbreak of war in the Middle East between Iran and the U.S. and Israel in late February 2026, and the seizures and attacks on vessels travelling through the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden, the Arabian Gulf, and the Strait of Hormuz, have caused supply disruptions and changes in trading patterns in the oil and gas markets and significant volatility in energy prices and spot charter hire rates.

We also expect the voyage expenses of the commercial pools in which we participate to be high in the near-term due to high bunker costs and being subject to additional war risks insurance premiums when the pool’s vessels transit through or call to any ports or areas or the waters of any country bordering the Arabian Gulf or the Red Sea.
For example, a catastrophic spill could exceed INSW’s $1.0 billion per vessel insurance coverage and have a material adverse effect on its operations.
To date, these geopolitical developments have not had a material adverse effect on INSW’s operations, financial condition, results of operations or cash flow.

risks.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Part II Item 1A Risk Factors.
risks.claim: U.S. and Chinese port-fee orders affecting Chinese-built or Chinese-financed vessels (including 13 owned Chinese-built vessels, four below the 55,000 dwt minimum) and U.S.-controlled entities could raise voyage costs if the 2025 one-year fee suspensions are not extended.
quotes: In addition, the United States issued regulations in October 2025 that certain vessels constructed in China or operated by a Chinese entity are charged a fee based on their net tonnage upon entering a U.S. port, which fee increases over time.

The Company currently owns 13 vessels that were constructed in China (four of which are below the 55,000 dwt minimum to which the U.S. fees apply), bareboat charters in one Chinese built vessel and has contracts to bareboat charter in three Chinese built newbuild vessels from a Chinese financial institution in a financing leasing arrangement, and bareboat charters in three non-Chinese built vessels from a Chinese financial institution in a financing leasing arrangement.
On November 10, 2025, the United States and China each suspended its port fee orders for one year.

The United States Trade Representative has proposed to extend the U.S. suspension through January 9, 2027, but the extension has not yet been finalized, and China has not yet formally announced a corresponding extension of its fee suspension.

risks.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Risk Factors and MD&A and the Q3 2026 earnings release.
risks.claim: The global tanker newbuilding orderbook expanded from 7% in 2023 to 14% in 2024 and 17% in 2025, which could depress spot charter rates and vessel values if new deliveries exceed vessel recycling.
quotes: The newbuilding order book of all classes of tankers (representing vessels in various stages of planning or construction that will be delivered in the future) equaled approximately 17%, 14% and 7% as of each of December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023.
When the number of new ships of a particular class delivered exceeds the number of vessels of that class being recycled over a period, available capacity in that class increases.

During the second half of 2025, tanker values increased, primarily because of higher TCE rates (resulting in part from geopolitical conditions) and limited shipyard capacity to construct tankers because of orders for other categories of vessels such as bulk carriers, container ships and LNG carriers.
